Docker vs Bun snapshot parity check
date: 2026-11-01   host: Darwin arm64   commit: origin/main a80bb93   oasdiff: v1.35.0

Goal: confirm that script/openapi-snapshot.sh (Bun, `serve`) produces exactly the spec our deployed
container publishes, so dropping the design doc's `docker compose up --build` loses nothing.

1) Original design-doc approach: our Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml, same as the VM deploy
$ docker compose up -d --build
  #3 load metadata for docker.io/oven/bun:1.3.14      DONE 1.4s
  #7 RUN apt-get update && apt-get install ...         CACHED (from an earlier attempt; not cached on a fresh CI runner)
  #9 COPY . .                                          DONE 0.9s
  #10 RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile                DONE 239.3s
  compose exit=0   build + up: 491s
$ until curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:4096/global/health; do sleep 2; done
  healthy after 8 attempt(s), 506s total
$ curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:4096/doc -o docker.json
$ docker compose down
Resulting image: 4.86GB, plus 5.16GB of build cache.
An earlier attempt on the same machine crashed Docker Desktop mid-build (disk nearly full).

2) Bun approach used by the workflow
$ ./script/openapi-snapshot.sh . bun.json
  Server is up after 3 attempt(s)
  Saved OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec with 162 paths to bun.json
  about 5s total

3) Comparison
$ shasum -a 256 docker.json bun.json
c3a9f94af0c3324d97b482b14c692e810ce7ccac3136319ba46334de972b4cf1  docker.json
c3a9f94af0c3324d97b482b14c692e810ce7ccac3136319ba46334de972b4cf1  bun.json
$ cmp docker.json bun.json
(no output: byte-identical, 478747 bytes each)
$ oasdiff breaking bun.json docker.json --fail-on ERR
No breaking changes to report, but the specs are different.   <- duplicate-tag quirk, see README.md
exit code: 0
$ oasdiff changelog bun.json docker.json
No changes to report, but the specs are different.
exit code: 0

Conclusion: the Bun snapshot is byte-identical to what the Docker container serves. Even with the apt layer
cached, one Docker snapshot took about 8.5 minutes versus about 5s with Bun. The check needs two snapshots, so a
cold Docker build would not fit the 15-minute job limit.
